<!-- Greeting -->
Hi @woderchen! I'm [Dosu](https://go.dosu.dev/dosubot) and I’m helping the sherpa-onnx team.

<!-- Answer -->
You're correct—on modern macOS, System Integrity Protection (SIP) prevents Electron apps from honoring DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH, which breaks dynamic loading of native modules like sherpa-onnx-node even if the environment variable is set. This is a known limitation for GUI apps on macOS, and the official documentation only suggests setting DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH, without addressing SIP or Electron-specific issues [source](https://k2-fsa.github.io/sherpa/onnx/pascal-api/index.html).

There isn't official guidance for Electron/macOS in sherpa-onnx docs, but the robust approach is to patch the dylib and .node files to use @loader_path or @rpath so dependencies are resolved relative to the module location. You can do this with `install_name_tool`:

```sh
install_name_tool -change @rpath/libsherpa-onnx-c-api.dylib @loader_path/libsherpa-onnx-c-api.dylib path/to/sherpa-onnx.node
```

Then, bundle the dylibs in the same directory as the .node file. This way, Electron will find the dependencies without needing DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH, and SIP won't interfere.

This workflow isn't documented by sherpa-onnx-node, so you'll need to add a post-install script or patch step in your build process. Static linking avoids these issues, but it's not always available for Node.js modules [source](https://k2-fsa.github.io/sherpa/ncnn/install/macos.html).

Let me know if you want a more detailed step-by-step for patching and bundling!

Can you share how you fix it?

sure，resolved the issue of Electron on macOS failing to load and use sherpa-onnx-node by applying the following two commands:
install_name_tool -change @rpath/sherpa-onnx.node @loader_path/sherpa-onnx.node path/to/sherpa-onnx.node
install_name_tool -change @rpath/libonnxruntime.1.17.1.dylib @loader_path/libonnxruntime.1.17.1.dylib path/to/sherpa-onnx.node
